tech_stack.persistence: R2DBC with Flyway migrations; embedded in-process substitute for boot/test only

module_layout.integration: Single deployable, single composition root at the base package. Contexts integrate only through the published events TelemetrySampleValidated, TelemetrySampleValidationFailed and TelemetrySampleBackfilled over in-process bounded reactive streams (Sinks with onBackpressureBuffer(capacity, false)); no context reads another's internals.

surfaces.traced_from: Ingestion entry point keeps backpressure control; context map: external -> Sample Ingestion & Validation

surfaces.traced_from: context map: Sample Ingestion & Validation -> Backfill Reordering & Windowing

surfaces.traced_from: context map: Backfill Reordering & Windowing -> external (streaming analytics consumers)

rules.statement: Every incoming 1Hz Telemetry Sample is validated before downstream propagation (HR 30-240 BPM, Power 0-2500W, Cadence 0-220 RPM, Swimming Pace >45 sec/100m)
Invalid samples are tagged VALIDATION_FAILED and the underlying payload is never dropped
Ingestion entry point keeps backpressure control with zero blocking I/O on thread pools under burst load (thousands of simultaneous 1Hz transmissions)
Backfill Reorder Window: 60-second window within which delayed out-of-order packets are re-indexed by t_device.
Ingress Timestamp (t_ingress): Arrival time at the ingestion entry point; never used for ordering.
Metrics without ranges (ground contact time, respiration, swim stroke telemetry) have no Sensor Metric Boundary stated; Swimming Pace has only a lower bound (>45 sec/100m), no upper bound.
Packets delayed up to 60 seconds are re-indexed chronologically on t_device rather than t_ingress
Raw time-series records are strictly append-only
Corrective streams or backfilled frames append new Event Revisions, never mutate history

storage_paradigm.primary: relational append-only event log (single reactive-accessible store, owned by Telemetry Event Log)
storage_paradigm.derived: none; window buffers in Backfill Reordering & Windowing are transient bounded in-memory state, rebuildable from the log

data_model.keys: surrogate id; natural lookup (device, metric, t_device)
invariants: VALIDATION_FAILED status stored as a tag, payload retained
data_model.sensitivity: athlete biometric/health data - classify, restrict access

data_model.keys: surrogate id; reference by id to the Raw Telemetry Record revised; revision sequence
invariants: corrections and backfills append new revisions, never overwrite
append-only; actor, action, outcome, timestamp, correlation id

queries: read history by (device, metric) ordered by t_device with keyset pagination, bounded results
persistence.performance: Batched reactive appends; no unbounded scans or offsets; index on (device, metric, t_device).
persistence.migration_plan: Ordered, recorded, expand-only Flyway scripts packaged on the classpath; embedded substitute only under the test profile.
persistence.backup_recovery: Periodic backup of the event log; restore by replay since history is append-only; owned by platform operations.
open_questions: Transport delivery semantics (at-most-once vs at-least-once) and dedup identity: is the value part of the identity, and what separates a retry from a correction revision?
Handling of samples later than the 60-second window (rejected or appended as backfill Event Revisions).
Ranges for ground contact time, respiration, swim stroke telemetry; Swimming Pace upper bound.

logs.consumer: external log shipper reads the file, never the app

export.metrics: actuator metrics only; no scrape or push target named
export.dependency: no runtime dependency on external tools; boot passes with them absent

risks: Unresolved retry vs correction identity in the append-only log
Handling of samples older than the 60-second window is unspecified
Metrics without ranges cannot be validated
Unbounded buffering under burst load must be avoided; bounded sinks with overflow duty
Sink termination under subscriber churn kills ingestion unless built with autoCancel=false
Reordering window held in memory loses state on restart; rebuildable from the log
